record.paper_title: Open problems in theory of nuclear open quantum systems
record.context_brief: States most affected by continuum coupling
record.original_question: In nuclear open quantum systems, how can one identify and predict which bound or unbound interacting-shell-model eigenstates are most strongly reorganized by coupling to scattering-continuum reaction channels, rather than assuming that continuum coupling produces a uniform instability of all states near a particle-emission threshold?

evidence.quote: Which nuclear states are most impacted by the coupling to the scattering continuum?
As shown above, |Ecorr| is both state- and system-dependent, i.e., the continuum coupling does not induce a global instability of all ISM eigenstates close to the particle emission threshold.
On the contrary, for those ISM wave functions which are susceptible to the continuum coupling, the near-threshold instability is seen predominantly in a single pair of unperturbed ISM states.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a nuclear many-body system modeled as an open quantum system in which a finite set of valence nucleons occupy single-particle orbitals built from a complete Berggren basis. The Berggren basis consists of bound states, narrow Gamow (resonance) states with complex energies, and a non-resonant scattering continuum, so that bound, resonant, and continuum single-particle states are treated on equal footing. The interacting shell model (ISM) Hamiltonian H_0 is defined by restricting all valence nucleons to bound (and possibly narrow resonance) orbitals; its eigenstates {|i⟩} are called ISM eigenstates. The full open-quantum-system Hamiltonian H = H_0 + V_c is obtained by adding the coupling V_c of the valence configurations to the scattering continuum reaction channels associated with one-nucleon decay channels c. For each ISM eigenstate |i⟩ with unperturbed energy E_i, define the continuum-coupling correlation energy

   E_corr(i) = ⟨i| V_c (E_i − Q H_0 Q)^{-1} Q V_c |i⟩,

where Q projects onto continuum configurations, evaluated near a particle-emission threshold E_th.

Provide a criterion, expressed in terms of the structure of the ISM wave functions |i⟩, the available decay channels c, and the threshold energy E_th, that identifies which ISM eigenstates are strongly reorganized by the coupling V_c (i.e., have anomalously large |E_corr(i)| and/or significant mixing with another specific ISM state) and which remain essentially unaffected. In particular, characterize the mechanism by which the near-threshold instability concentrates within a single pair of unperturbed ISM eigenstates rather than producing a uniform destabilization of all ISM eigenstates lying close to E_th, and predict, prior to performing a full Gamow-shell-model diagonalization, which pair of states will be selected for a given nucleus and threshold.
artifact.status_search_result: Subsequent Gamow-shell-model studies (notably a 2024 study of the continuum-coupling correlation energy near particle-emission thresholds) have provided systematic numerical evidence that the continuum-coupling correlation energy is state- and system-dependent, increases with the number of valence nucleons, is larger in even-even isotopes, and that near-threshold instability is dominated by a single pair of unperturbed ISM states whose decay channel matches the channel opening at threshold. However, no fully predictive analytic criterion that identifies the affected pair without performing a GSM calculation appears to be established; the question therefore appears partially solved.

status_evidence.title: Behavior of the continuum coupling correlation energy in the vicinity of the particle emission threshold — Gamow shell model study
status_evidence.snippet: The continuum-coupling correlation energy is shown to be state- and system-dependent, with the strongest effects concentrated in specific pairs of unperturbed ISM states whose structure matches the opening decay channel.
status_evidence.claim: Provides numerical characterization (state- and system-dependence) of which ISM eigenstates are most affected by continuum coupling near particle-emission thresholds.

status_evidence.title: Recent Progress in Gamow Shell Model Calculations of Drip Line Nuclei
status_evidence.snippet: Reviews how the Berggren ensemble and Gamow shell model account for continuum coupling and clustering of near-threshold states.
status_evidence.claim: Confirms that selective near-threshold reorganization of states is observed across drip-line nuclei but a closed-form predictive criterion is not given.
